about: Internal review record read by apps/agent/scripts/finalize.ts into docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md. Findings are written by the reviewers; counts and tables are generated from this file. Internal review by the YINGLONG team; no third-party audit has been performed.

findings.title: Starting a sign-up with an existing account's public key reset that account
findings.description: POST /v1/visitors overwrote the stored visitor record (new session token, sealed flag cleared) before any signature proved control of the key. The passkey public key and the secret-key owner address are public, so anyone could start such a sign-up.
findings.impact: Denial of service: the real owner's session stopped working and log in again refused the account until it sealed again. No funds or authority could be taken: sealing still needs the key.
findings.recommendation: Keep a sealed account's record and session unchanged until the new seal verifies on the account itself.
findings.resolution: The pending sign-up now holds its own record and token; the stored record is replaced only after the seal verifies (ERC-1271 on the account). apps/agent/scripts/visitor-key-e2e.mts re-registers an address as a stranger would and still logs in and pays.

findings.title: Login challenge did not bind the issue time and chain id it handed out
findings.description: Only the nonce and its expiry were stored; the signed message was rebuilt from the issue time sent back by the client and the chain id of the account's ledger.
findings.impact: Low: the nonce was already single-use and expired after 5 minutes, so replay was not possible; the message a user signed could differ from the one issued.
findings.recommendation: Store the issue time and chain id with the nonce and rebuild the message from the stored values.
findings.resolution: Challenges store {expires, issuedAt, chainId}; a mismatching issue time or ledger is refused.

findings.title: A co-sign approval was created for a payment the ledger refuses for another reason
findings.description: When the simulation reverted for a reason other than the missing co-signature (for example VelocityExceeded), an escalated request still produced an approval request.
findings.impact: The user could approve a payment that would then revert on chain: a confusing approval, no loss of funds (the enforcers refuse it).
findings.recommendation: Create an approval only when the simulation succeeds or fails solely with CoSignRequired.
findings.resolution: The approval is created only for an approvable simulation.

findings.title: The web signing guard allows a user operation without decoding its calls
findings.description: PackedUserOperation is on the allowlist for seal, resume and revoke, but the guard does not decode the inner calls against an allowlist, and an unknown message kind from the network throws instead of returning a typed refusal.
findings.impact: The guard relies on the page's own decoding of what the user is shown; a compromised service could ask the passkey to sign a user operation with other calls. The account's enforcers still bound what an agent can do, and the user sees the decoded operation before signing.
findings.recommendation: Decode the user operation's execution calls and accept only the publish, delegation, pause, resume and revoke calls to known contracts; return a typed refusal for unknown kinds.
findings.resolution: Planned before submission (owner: front end with back end).

findings.title: MandateRegistry.canExecute reports no live mandate after the newer of two live mandates is revoked
findings.description: One liveMandateOfAgent slot per account and agent, while two lineages may each hold a live mandate; revoking the newer one clears the slot although the older one is still live (test_finding_canExecuteAfterRevokingNewerOfTwoLiveMandates, skipped).
findings.impact: View only: the read interface answers (false, NO_LIVE_MANDATE) for an agent that can still redeem. Enforcement is unaffected: MandateBindingEnforcer checks each mandate's own status.
findings.recommendation: Track live mandates per lineage, or recompute the slot on revoke.
findings.wontfixReason: The deployed bytecode is frozen and cited by the execution evidence on two ledgers; the defect affects a read-only helper, not enforcement. Fix in the next contract version.

findings.title: ProductRegistry.allProducts lists a product twice after delist and relist
findings.description: list() appends to the product array whenever the product is not currently listed, so delist followed by list duplicates it (test_finding_relistAfterDelistDuplicatesAllProducts, skipped).
findings.impact: View only: allProducts() returns duplicates. Suitability enforcement reads the product mapping and is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Append only on the first listing, or de-duplicate in the view.
findings.wontfixReason: Frozen, evidence-cited bytecode; read-only helper; the front end de-duplicates.

findings.title: Logging in on a second device ends the first device's session
findings.description: Each login issues a new session token and stores only its hash, replacing the previous one.
findings.impact: Usability: the first device is logged out without notice. No security impact.
findings.recommendation: Keep a small set of session hashes per visitor, or tell the user that other devices were signed out.

findings.title: Login challenges and sign-ups in progress are kept in memory
findings.description: Open login challenges and pending seals live in process memory.
findings.impact: A service restart asks a visitor in the middle of a login or sign-up to start it again. No data is lost: sealed accounts are stored on disk and on chain.
findings.recommendation: Persist them with their expiry if restarts become frequent.
findings.wontfixReason: Both expire within 15 minutes; a restart costs one retry and keeps the attack surface small.
